stage_a.note: Strong positive expression. Positive, enthusiastic engagement characterizes most of the presentation.
Sustained engagement with the subject is evident across much of the presentation.
Friendly, approachable and considerate expression characterizes much of the presentation.

venture.description: An online marketplace for renting private swimming pools by the hour.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim introduces Swimply, an app for renting private pools by the hour, and demonstrates booking a pool for Jesse.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that he is not getting in the pool with Jesse.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks if the business is real.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim confirms that the business is real.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks to confirm that the business is essentially an Airbnb for swimming pools.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim agrees with Lori's comparison.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks if the app is live and requests numbers on downloads, users, and revenue.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara asks how many pools are currently on the platform.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks who originally came up with the idea for the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim shares the origin story of making a deal with his neighbor to rent her pool for his family.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin admits he initially thought the idea was crazy, but hearing the story makes it seem even crazier.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim laughs and agrees that the idea is crazy.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks Bunim to explain what happened next in the business's development.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim explains using his Bar Mitzvah money to launch a website and knocking on doors to get the first pools.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks how much of his initial money he burned through.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim states he spent ten thousand dollars initially, then raised thirty thousand to keep the site running.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that he is worried Bunim is going to spontaneously combust from talking so fast.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks Bunim to confirm his earlier statement about booking nine hundred hours.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim confirms nine hundred hours were booked, getting their first hundred pools and raising nine hundred sixty thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks to confirm that Bunim raised nine hundred sixty thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim confirms the fundraising amount.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks how much equity was sold to raise that capital.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim states the money was raised at a six million dollar valuation.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks how Bunim managed to achieve that valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim begins to explain that a pool maintenance partnership reached out to them.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks how many hours have been booked year to date.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim deflects to explain that after raising the money, they had to develop a proper website that could scale.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks if this is his third attempt at developing a proper website.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim claims this is the first real attempt, downplaying the previous two websites.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark points out that the previous attempts still count because they cost forty thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim concedes the point and explains they tried to build the app in three months, leading to malfunctions.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara tells Bunim to take a breath because he is speaking so quickly.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim answers Mark's earlier question, stating they booked sixteen hundred individual hours year to date.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks Bunim to walk through the financial model and explain what the pool owner charges and what Swimply makes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim explains hosts set their own prices, and Swimply takes a fifteen percent commission plus a ten percent fee.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark confirms that the total fee taken by Swimply is twenty-five percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim confirms the total is twenty-five percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks how much money the company has made year to date.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim states they did around two hundred fifteen thousand dollars in marketplace revenue.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks if that figure is gross or net revenue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim clarifies it is gross revenue and their net is around twenty percent of that.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark calculates and asks to confirm that the net revenue is forty-two thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim confirms the net revenue figure.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert expresses amazement that Bunim raised a million dollars for this idea.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara argues that the high valuation makes no sense based on their current revenue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim defends the valuation by saying it is a game of scale, promise, and vision.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara counters that it is also a game of money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim briefly agrees with Barbara's point.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori explains she doesn't want to invest despite seeing empty pools when flying, and she exits.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks where people go to the bathroom when they show up at a rented pool.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim explains that half of the hosts offer a way to use a side door for bathroom access.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks what the second option is for bathrooms.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim states the second option is not offering a bathroom at all.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin suggests that without a bathroom, people will just pee in the pool.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim jokes that Jesse is probably peeing in the pool right now.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara notes she hasn't heard what people are willing to pay for an hour of pool time.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim begins to answer by saying there is a range of prices.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara adds a second question about whether customers return weekly or if it's a one-time event.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim answers the pricing question, stating the average went from forty-five to ninety dollars an hour.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks how many people typically come over for a hundred-dollar booking.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim states the average group size increased from seven last year to twelve this year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara says the idea is nuts, she doesn't get it, and calls Bunim a fast talker before exiting.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark sees the value for parties but questions how often people will do it and how it scales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim explains that when the price was lower, seventy percent of bookings were families.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks about the demographics for the current year since the family stat was from the beta.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim explains they added a chat feature to facilitate parties but ran into technical issues with notifications.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin states the valuation is nuts given the low revenue and technical problems, and he exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim projects breaking even next year and profiting fifteen million the year after to defend the valuation.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks if the fifteen million figure is gross revenue or overall profits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim clarifies that the fifteen million figure represents their profits.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks to confirm that he means profits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim confirms profits and projects two hundred eighty-nine million in gross revenue by 2022.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark tells Bunim that while excitement is good, he lacks self-awareness and is lying to himself.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim defends his awareness by citing that six hundred seventy-five thousand dollars of business went through the platform.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark argues that just because there is volume doesn't mean the business model scales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim insists there is potential and blames the low capitalization on solvable technical issues.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark states that Bunim's pricing and reality are in two different universes, and he exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim nervously asks Mark if he is sure about his decision.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark confirms that he is sure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim appeals to Mark, mentioning his young age and history of starting businesses to prove his hustle.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark acknowledges that Bunim is a hustler.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim asks the remaining sharks if the projections are what is bothering them.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark tells Bunim that projections are worthless and he should focus on the remaining sharks.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert admits he initially thought the idea was crazy but now sees it could help people.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim greets Robert.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert argues that projecting two hundred eighty-nine million in three years is crazy and non-linear.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim defends the projections by stating that startups grow through scale and rapid growth.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks how many companies actually go from zero to two hundred eighty-nine million in three years.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin answers Robert's question, stating that zero companies achieve that growth.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim disagrees and points to their proof of concept and optimized pools as evidence of potential.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert says he loves Bunim's passion but feels it is too early to invest, so he exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim mentions his age again, suggesting he needs help to figure out the business operations.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert tells Bunim that his age is not an excuse.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim agrees it's not an excuse but emphasizes that he is learning every day.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert expresses exasperation and repeats that he is out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim thanks the sharks as the pitch concludes.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin thanks Bunim.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Bunim tells Jesse he hopes he doesn't freeze getting out of the pool.

exchanges.label: Is the business real and live
Origin story and number of pools

decisions.note: Sees empty pools but does not want to invest despite the need.
Thinks the idea is nuts, does not get it, calls the founder a fast talker.
Thinks the valuation is nuts given the low revenue and technical problems.
Believes the pricing and reality are disconnected and the founder lacks self-awareness.
Loves the passion but feels it is too early to invest.
